question: Room heat loss
speechText: Right, that room’s losing about 1.4 kW at design temp. You’ll need a rad that can hit that at 45 degrees, not 70.
displayText:
### 📐 Room Heat Loss Calculation

• **Design Load**: 1.4 kW at -3°C external design temperature.
• **Flow Target**: Sized at **45°C flow** (Delta-T 30), not legacy 70°C.
• **Action**: Verify room dimension and U-values on NSAI SR50 table.

question: Undersized radiator
speechText: That rad’s too small for low-temp heating. You’ll need to bump it up a size or go double-panel.
displayText:
### ⚠️ Undersized Radiator Remediation

• **Issue**: Output at 45°C drops by ~50% compared to 75°C catalogue ratings.
• **Solution**: Upgrade to double-panel convector (Type 22) or increase length by 30%.
• **Grant Rule**: Ensures room reaches 21°C comfort setpoint.

question: Oversized radiator
speechText: That one’s oversized. It’ll work, but it’s costing the homeowner more than needed. I’ll give you the proper output.
displayText:
### 🔍 Radiator Oversizing Audit

• **Status**: Exceeds required room heat loss by >40%.
• **Impact**: Causes minor thermal overshoot and unnecessary capital cost.
• **Proper Output**: Calculated precisely at Delta-T 30.

question: Quick heat loss check
speechText: Give me the room dimensions and window type — I’ll run the heat loss in seconds.
displayText:
### ⚡ Rapid Room Heat Loss Tool

• **Inputs Needed**: Room Length × Width × Height (m), wall construction, and glazing type.
• **Output**: Room loss in Watts and minimum Delta-T30 radiator sizing.

question: Flow temperature advice
speechText: Keep it around 45 degrees for heat pumps. Anything higher and you’re losing efficiency.
displayText:
### 🌡️ Flow Temperature Optimization

• **Optimal Flow**: 45°C flow ($	ext{COP} \ge 3.8$).
• **Efficiency Loss**: Every 5°C increase in flow temperature reduces seasonal COP by ~7%.
• **NSAI Rule**: Design for 45°C on radiators and 35°C on underfloor.

question: Pipework check
speechText: Your pipework looks grand — 16mm is fine for most runs. I’ll flag any bottlenecks.
displayText:
### 🚰 Distribution Pipe Sizing Audit

• **Branch Runs**: 16mm multilayer or 15mm copper suitable for up to 1.8 kW heat loads.
• **Main Headers**: 22mm or 28mm copper required for high flow rates.
• **Velocity**: Maintained under $0.8	ext{ m/s}$ to eliminate turbulence.

question: Balancing issues
speechText: If the room’s slow to heat, it’s usually balancing. Quick job — nothing dramatic.
displayText:
### ⚖️ Hydraulic System Balancing

• **Symptom**: Distant radiators take hours to warm up.
• **Fix**: Adjust lockshield valves to ensure uniform return temperatures across all circuits ($\Delta T pprox 5	ext{-}7^{\circ}	ext{C}$).

question: Double vs single panel
speechText: Go double-panel if the room needs the extra wattage. No point in guessing — I’ll give you the numbers.
displayText:
### 🔄 Type 11 (Single) vs Type 22 (Double) Rads

• **Type 11**: Single panel, low convective surface area.
• **Type 22**: Double panel, double convector (+80% output for identical wall length).
• **Recommendation**: Upgrade Type 11 to Type 22 when wall width is constrained.

question: Radiator output tables
speechText: I’ll give you the exact output at 45°C, not the catalogue number at 70°C. Makes a big difference.
displayText:
### 📊 True Delta-T 30 Output Table

• **Catalogue Rating**: Calculated at $\Delta T 50^{\circ}	ext{C}$ (75°C flow).
• **True Low-Temp Rating**: $	ext{Watts}_{45^{\circ}	ext{C}} = 	ext{Catalogue Watts} 	imes 0.51$.
• **Standard**: Eliminates cold-room callbacks.

question: Old radiators
speechText: Some of these older rads are fine. We’ll only replace what’s actually undersized.
displayText:
### 🛠️ Existing Radiator Retention Check

• **Audit First**: Keep oversized existing rads if they meet Delta-T 30 load requirements.
• **Savings**: Homeowner saves €180–€300 per retained radiator.
• **Requirement**: Chemical flush and magnetic filter installation mandatory.

question: Aluminium radiators
speechText: Aluminium heats fast but drops fast. Steel panels are grand for heat pumps.
displayText:
### 🧲 Aluminium vs Steel Radiators

• **Aluminium**: Fast thermal response, low water content, higher material cost.
• **Steel Panels**: Higher thermal inertia, ideal for continuous low-temperature heat pump operation.

question: Towel rails
speechText: Towel rails are decorative — they don’t heat rooms. You’ll need a proper rad in there.
displayText:
### 🚿 Bathroom Heating & Towel Rails

• **Reality**: Ladder towel rails deliver under 250 Watts at 45°C flow.
• **Best Practice**: Add dedicated compact radiator or underfloor electric mat for primary space heating.
citation: NSAI SR50 Bathroom Space Heating Standards

question: Heat pump sizing
speechText: That house needs about 6 kW. Don’t oversize — it’ll short-cycle and annoy everyone.
displayText:
### ⚡ Heat Pump Capacity Sizing

• **Calculated Heat Loss**: 5.4 kW at -3°C external load.
• **Recommended Unit**: **6 kW inverter monobloc**.
• **Why Not 10 kW**: Oversizing causes compressor short-cycling, high standby draw, and premature wear.
citation: NSAI SR50-2 Heat Pump Sizing Rules

question: SR50 compliance
speechText: SR50 just means the system is designed properly — rads, pipework, and heat pump all matched. I’ll check it for you.
displayText:
### 📜 NSAI SR50 Compliance Sign-Off

• **Core Standard**: NSAI SR50 Code of Practice for domestic wet central heating systems.
• **Checks**: Flow temperature, radiator Delta-T, system water volume, hydraulic balancing, and insulation.

question: Buffer tank
speechText: You don’t need a buffer tank unless the layout demands it. I’ll tell you straight.
displayText:
### 🛢️ Buffer Tank vs Direct Volumiser

• **Direct Connection**: Prefer direct connection with a 25–50L volumiser bottle if 2+ circuits are open.
• **Buffer Tank**: Only needed on highly zoned, multi-manifold systems with complex secondary mixing circuits.

question: Flow temp too high
speechText: If you’re running at 55 or 60 degrees, something’s off. We’ll fix the sizing.
displayText:
### ⚠️ High Flow Temperature Diagnosis

• **Threshold**: If operating flow $> 50^{\circ}	ext{C}$ in mild weather ($> 5^{\circ}	ext{C}$ ambient).
• **Root Cause**: Severely undersized radiators or incorrect weather compensation curve.
• **Fix**: Resize bottleneck radiators to drop flow back to 45°C.

question: Outdoor unit placement
speechText: Stick it somewhere with airflow and low echo. Modern units are quiet enough.
displayText:
### 🏡 Outdoor Monobloc Placement

• **Clearances**: Minimum 300mm rear clearance, 1,000mm front clearance for unhindered airflow.
• **Acoustics**: Avoid narrow alcoves or mounting under bedroom windows.

question: Defrost cycles
speechText: Defrost is normal — don’t panic. If it’s happening too often, we’ll check the setup.
displayText:
### ❄️ Defrost Cycle Operation

• **Normal Operation**: Occurs in cold, humid weather (0°C to 4°C ambient) every 45–90 minutes.
• **Excessive Defrost**: Indicates restricted evaporator airflow or low refrigerant charge.

question: Heat pump brand differences
speechText: They’re all grand once sized right. The design matters more than the badge.
displayText:
### 🏷️ Heat Pump Manufacturer Assessment

• **Key Metric**: Seasonal Coefficient of Performance ($	ext{SCOP} \ge 4.2$).
• **Reality**: System design, low flow temperature, and hydraulic balancing determine 85% of real-world efficiency.

question: Hybrid systems
speechText: Hybrid is only worth it in certain cases. Most homes are fine with full heat pump.
displayText:
### 🔄 Hybrid Heat Pump vs Full Retrofit

• **Hybrid**: Retains existing gas/oil boiler for sub-zero peak loads.
• **Full Heat Pump**: Unlocks maximum SEAI grants (€6,500–€12,500) and completely eliminates fossil fuels.

question: Hot water cylinder
speechText: You’ll need a proper cylinder for heat pumps — the old coil ones won’t cut it.
displayText:
### 🛢️ Heat Pump Domestic Hot Water Cylinder

• **Requirement**: High-surface-area internal heat exchanger coil ($\ge 2.5	ext{ m}^2$).
• **Legacy Boiler Cylinders**: $0.8	ext{ m}^2$ coils cannot transfer heat at 50°C flow, leading to extreme reheat times.

question: Noise concerns
speechText: Modern units are fridge-quiet. Placement matters more than the brand.
displayText:
### 🔇 Acoustic Performance Standards

• **Sound Pressure**: Modern inverter units operate at 42–48 dB(A) at 1 metre.
• **Boundary Compliance**: Must meet $< 43	ext{ dB(A)}$ at neighboring property boundaries.
citation: Irish Planning & Building Regulations Part L

question: Weather compensation
speechText: Use weather comp — it’s free efficiency. Keeps the flow temp nice and steady.
displayText:
### 📈 Weather Compensation Curves

• **Function**: Automatically modulates flow temperature based on outdoor sensor readings.
• **Mild Weather (10°C)**: Lowers flow to 35°C ($	ext{COP} pprox 4.8$).
• **Cold Weather (-3°C)**: Increases flow to 45°C.

question: Installer mistakes
speechText: The biggest mistake is oversizing. We’ll avoid that by doing the numbers properly.
displayText:
### 🚫 Top 3 Heat Pump Installation Pitfalls

1. **Oversizing the unit** (leads to short-cycling and premature failure).
2. **Leaving legacy boiler cylinders** in place (poor hot water recovery).
3. **Skipping low-temp radiator sizing** (results in cold rooms).

question: Pipe diameter
speechText: 16mm is fine for most runs. If you’ve long circuits, we’ll check pressure drop.
displayText:
### 📐 Pipe Diameter & Flow Velocity

• **Standard Runs**: 16mm multilayer handles up to 1.8 kW at $\Delta T 5^{\circ}	ext{C}$.
• **Long Circuit Runs**: Upgrade to 20mm to avoid excessive circuit pressure drops ($> 25	ext{ kPa}$).

question: Manifold layout
speechText: Manifolds are handy for zoning. I’ll tell you if it’s worth adding.
displayText:
### 🔀 Manifold vs Traditional Tee Plumbing

• **Manifolds**: Provide dedicated individual pipe runs, zero joint leaks under floors, and built-in flowmeters.
• **Tee System**: Suitable for standard retrofits when existing pipework is sound.

question: Thermostats
speechText: Smart stats help, but the main thing is proper flow temp. Controls won’t fix bad sizing.
displayText:
### 🎛️ Thermostatic Controls & Smart Stats

• **Principle**: Heating controls provide scheduling and setback temperatures.
• **Rule**: Controls cannot compensate for undersized radiators or incorrect water flow rates.

question: TRVs
speechText: TRVs are grand, but don’t choke the system. Keep the main circuit open.
displayText:
### 🛑 Thermostatic Radiator Valves (TRVs)

• **Bypass Rule**: Keep at least 2 primary radiators (hallway/bathrooms) without TRVs to maintain minimum water circulation.
• **Alternative**: Automatic differential pressure bypass valve.

question: Circulation pump
speechText: Make sure the pump can handle low-temp flow. I’ll check the curve.
displayText:
### 🔄 Circulation Pump Sizing

• **Heat Pump Flow**: Requires higher flow rates ($\Delta T = 5^{\circ}	ext{C}$ vs $\Delta T = 20^{\circ}	ext{C}$ on gas boilers).
• **Pump Curve**: High-efficiency variable speed pump with $\ge 6	ext{m}$ head recommended.

question: Zoning
speechText: Heat pumps prefer fewer zones. Keep it simple — steady heat wins.
displayText:
### 🏠 Heat Pump Zoning Strategy

• **Ideal**: 2 simple zones (Living / Sleeping) or open-plan steady-state.
• **Over-Zoning**: Micro-zoning every room causes heat pumps to hunt and short-cycle.

question: Return temperature
speechText: Keep the return temp low — that’s where the efficiency comes from.
displayText:
### 📉 Return Temperature Management

• **Target**: $\Delta T$ of $5^{\circ}	ext{C}$ to $7^{\circ}	ext{C}$ (e.g. 45°C flow, 38°C–40°C return).
• **Impact**: Lower return temperature maximizes refrigerant sub-cooling and system COP.

question: Pipe insulation
speechText: Insulate everything. Bare pipes are just heating the attic.
displayText:
### 🛡️ Thermal Pipe Insulation

• **Requirement**: Minimum 19mm–25mm wall thickness closed-cell insulation on all unheated space runs (attics/crawlspaces).
• **External Monobloc Runs**: UV-resistant, weatherproof insulation mandatory.
citation: Building Regulations Part L & NSAI SR50

question: Cylinder coil
speechText: Make sure the coil is heat-pump rated. Old coils take forever.
displayText:
### 🛢️ Cylinder Coil Surface Area

• **Heat Pump Coil**: Minimum $2.5	ext{ m}^2$ internal surface area.
• **Heat Transfer**: Allows 50°C heat pump flow to reheat a 200L tank in under 45 minutes.

question: Flow balancing
speechText: Balance the rads properly — it’s the difference between cosy and cranky.
displayText:
### ⚖️ Commissioning Flow Balancing

• **Procedure**: Set flow rates across every circuit using lockshields or manifold flow meters.
• **Result**: Every room receives its exact designed wattage simultaneously.

question: Solar sizing
speechText: 4 to 6 kWp suits most homes. I’ll check shading and pitch.
displayText:
### ☀️ Solar PV Array Sizing

• **Standard Array**: 10 to 14 panels (4.4 kWp – 6.0 kWp).
• **Annual Generation**: 4,200 to 5,500 kWh/year under Irish irradiance.
• **Grant**: €2,100 SEAI Solar PV grant available.

question: Diverter
speechText: A diverter is great — free hot water in summer.
displayText:
### ⚡ Solar Immersion Diverter (eddi / Solar iBoost)

• **Function**: Diverts excess solar export directly to the hot water immersion coil.
• **Benefit**: Zero-cost domestic hot water from April through October.

question: Battery sizing
speechText: A 5 kWh battery is grand for most homes. Bigger only if they’re heavy users.
displayText:
### 🔋 Battery Storage Sizing

• **Optimal Size**: 5.12 kWh to 10.24 kWh LiFePO4 battery pack.
• **Self-Consumption**: Bumps solar self-consumption from 40% up to 85%.

question: Night-rate charging
speechText: Charge the battery at night and use it during the day — lovely savings.
displayText:
### 🌙 Night-Rate Battery Arbitrage

• **Night Rate (EV Tariff)**: ~7c – 11c / kWh (2 AM – 5 AM).
• **Day Rate**: ~34c – 38c / kWh.
• **Savings**: ~€750/year in pure grid arbitrage alone.

question: Inverter choice
speechText: Hybrid inverter keeps things tidy. Less boxes, less hassle.
displayText:
### 🔌 Hybrid vs AC-Coupled Inverters

• **Hybrid Inverter**: Manages both solar PV DC inputs and battery storage in a single compact enclosure.
• **AC-Coupled**: Preferred when retrofitting a battery to an existing pre-installed solar array.

question: Export payments
speechText: CEG pays well enough — but self-use is where the real savings are.
displayText:
### 💶 Clean Export Guarantee (CEG)

• **Export Tariff**: ~21c – 24c / kWh paid by Irish suppliers for exported power.
• **Priority**: Self-consumption (displacing 36c retail power) yields 50% greater financial value than export.

question: Solar + heat pump
speechText: They work great together. Solar knocks a chunk off the running costs.
displayText:
### ⚡ Solar PV + Heat Pump Synergy

• **Synergy**: Solar PV powers the heat pump compressor and domestic hot water generation.
• **DEAP 4.2.2**: Dual installation propels homes straight into the A1 / A2 BER band.

question: Roof suitability
speechText: If the roof has decent pitch and no shading, you’re laughing.
displayText:
### 🏠 Roof Orientation & Pitch Sizing

• **Ideal**: South-facing, 30°–40° pitch (100% yield).
• **East/West**: 82%–86% yield (generates broad morning/evening generation profile).

question: Cold room
speechText: If one room’s cold, it’s usually the rad. Quick swap and you’re sorted.
displayText:
### ❄️ Single Cold Room Troubleshooting

1. Check if radiator is sized for 45°C flow.
2. Check lockshield valve balancing.
3. Bleed air from top valve.
4. Upgrade to double-panel convector if heat loss exceeds output.

question: High bills
speechText: High bills mean high flow temp. We’ll bring it down.
displayText:
### 💶 High Energy Bill Diagnostics

• **Common Culprit**: Flow temperature set above 50°C or immersion heater operating constantly.
• **Remedy**: Re-engage weather compensation curve and verify heat pump cylinder sensor calibration.

question: Noisy pipes
speechText: Probably air or flow rate. Easy fix.
displayText:
### 🔊 Pipework Acoustic Diagnostics

• **Clicking/Ticking**: Pipe thermal expansion against joists (notch clearances needed).
• **Hissing/Whistling**: Water velocity $> 1.0	ext{ m/s}$ (modulate circulation pump down).

question: Slow heating
speechText: Heat pumps heat steady, not fast. Check the rad sizing.
displayText:
### ⏳ Slow Heat-Up Time Analysis

• **Design Principle**: Heat pumps maintain steady continuous warmth rather than rapid fossil boiler blast heating.
• **Verification**: Confirm radiator sizing supports low-flow delta-T.

question: Short cycling
speechText: Oversized unit. We’ll fix it with proper design.
displayText:
### 🔄 Compressor Short-Cycling Fix

• **Issue**: Unit starts and stops every few minutes.
• **Root Cause**: Oversized heat pump or low system water volume.
• **Solution**: Increase minimum open volume with volumiser or widen thermostat deadband differential.

question: Poor hot water
speechText: Old cylinder coil. Swap it for a heat-pump coil.
displayText:
### 🚿 Domestic Hot Water Recovery Diagnostics

• **Symptom**: Water takes hours to reach 50°C.
• **Root Cause**: Legacy standard cylinder with small $0.8	ext{ m}^2$ coil.
• **Fix**: Replace with dedicated heat-pump cylinder ($\ge 2.5	ext{ m}^2$ coil).

question: Radiator cold at bottom
speechText: Sludge. Needs a flush.
displayText:
### 🧪 Magnetite Sludge Accumulation

• **Symptom**: Radiator hot across top, cold in center/bottom.
• **Remedy**: Power flush system and install a high-capacity magnetic inline filter on primary return.

question: System keeps tripping
speechText: Could be pump load or wiring. We’ll check the basics first.
displayText:
### ⚡ Electrical & Breaker Trip Diagnostics

• **Check 1**: Dedicated Type B RCBO breaker installed for inverter heat pump compressor.
• **Check 2**: Rotary isolator wiring and immersion backup heater circuit load.
citation: ETCI National Rules for Electrical Installations
